title: Sorting out problems
goal: Return a wrong order, get a refund or exchange from customer care, report a lost phone to the police, stay calm but firm — and tell your friends exactly what everyone said.
intro:
Sooner or later something goes wrong: the parcel has the wrong saree in it, the shop won't exchange the shoes, an auto driver overcharges you, your phone disappears on a Mo Bus. This unit gives you the Odia to sort it out — describing the problem, asking for a return or an exchange, pushing politely for a supervisor, filing a report at the police station — and to keep your cool while you do it.

It also completes **reported speech**, because half of every problem is retelling it: 'they *said* the money would come back in seven days', 'he *told me to* wait', 'she *asked whether* I had the bill', 'they've *promised* to send the right one'. Odia does this with **ଯେ** and **ବୋଲି**, the **-ବାକୁ** form for instructions, and **କଥା ଦେବା** for promises.

vocab.en: to order (have something sent), get delivered
vocab.note: Causative of ମାଗିବା 'ask for': ଅନଲାଇନ୍ ମଗାଇଥିଲି 'I ordered it online'. Many people also say ଅର୍ଡର କରିବା.
ଫେରସ୍ତ କରିବା = to return (something); ଫେରସ୍ତ ହେବା = to be returnable/returned.
After the noun: ଏହା ବଦଳରେ 'instead of this'.
ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ = as per the rules — the phrase every helpline uses.
ସମାଧାନ କରିବା = to solve, sort out; ସମାଧାନ ହେବା = to get sorted.

vocab.en: to agree to, accept; to obey
vocab.note: With -ବାକୁ: ଫେରାଇବାକୁ ମାନିଲେ 'they agreed to refund'; ମାନିଲେ ନାହିଁ 'they refused'.
Often ironic: ଖାଲି ଆଶ୍ୱାସନା 'nothing but promises'.

vocab.en: FIR (first information report to the police)

vocab.note: ମୋତେ ଠକିଦେଲା = he ripped me off.
ମୋର କ୍ଷତି ହେଲା = I lost out.
ଦାବି କରିବା = to demand, to claim.
ପାଟି = mouth; ପାଟି କରିବା = to raise your voice.
କିଛି ଲାଭ ନାହିଁ = there's no point.

grammar.title: Reported speech in full: what they said and asked
grammar.body:
Unit 20 gave you the two patterns: **verb + ଯେ + clause** (ସେ କହିଲେ ଯେ …) and the more typically Odia **clause + ବୋଲି + verb** (… ବୋଲି କହିଲେ). Sorting out a problem means retelling all day, so here are the details.

**1. The tense stays as it was said.** ସେ କହିଲେ ଦୁଇ ଦିନରେ ଟଙ୍କା **ଫେରିବ** — literally 'they said the money *will* come back in two days'. English shifts to 'would'; Odia doesn't. Likewise ସେ କହିଲେ ଦୋକାନ ବନ୍ଦ **ଅଛି** 'he said the shop *was* shut'.

**2. Pronouns shift to your point of view**, as in English: the agent said 'I'll call you' → ସେ **ମୋତେ** ଫୋନ କରିବେ ବୋଲି କହିଲେ 'he said he'd call me'. With ବୋଲି, people also often keep the original words almost like a quotation: ସେ 'କାଲି ଆସନ୍ତୁ' ବୋଲି କହିଲେ.

**3. Reported questions.** Yes/no questions take **କି ନାହିଁ** 'whether (or not)': ସେ ପଚାରିଲେ ମୋ ପାଖରେ ବିଲ୍ ଅଛି **କି ନାହିଁ** 'she asked whether I had the bill'. Question-word questions just keep the question word, in place: ମୁଁ ପଚାରିଲି ପାର୍ସଲ୍ **କେବେ** ଆସିବ 'I asked when the parcel would come'. ବୋଲି works here too: କେବେ ଆସିବ ବୋଲି ପଚାରିଲି.

**4. 'He was saying…'** In relaxed retelling the past continuous **କହୁଥିଲେ / କହୁଥିଲା** is the normal reporting verb: ଦୋକାନୀ କହୁଥିଲା ୱାରେଣ୍ଟି ସରିଯାଇଛି 'the shopkeeper was saying the warranty's run out'.

**5. Hearsay**: **… ବୋଲି ଶୁଣିଲି** 'I heard that …'.

The trap: don't backshift. ~~ସେ କହିଲେ ଟଙ୍କା ଫେରିଥିଲା~~ means 'he said the money *had* come back', not 'would come back'.

grammar.title: Told me to…, agreed to…, promised: reporting requests and promises
grammar.body:
**Told me to do something**: the **-ବାକୁ** form + **କହିବା**, with the person told in the dative: ପୋଲିସ **ମୋତେ** ଥାନାକୁ ଆସି**ବାକୁ** କହିଲେ 'the police told me to come to the station'. The same frame works with **ଅନୁରୋଧ କରିବା** 'to request' (ମୁଁ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଟଙ୍କା ଫେରାଇବାକୁ ଅନୁରୋଧ କଲି 'I asked him to refund the money') and **ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା** 'to advise'.

**Told me not to**: **ନ** before the -ବାକୁ form: ବୋଉ ମୋତେ ଏକୁଟିଆ **ନ ଯିବାକୁ** କହିଲେ 'Mum told me not to go alone'.

**Agreed / refused to**: -ବାକୁ + **ମାନିବା**: ଦୋକାନୀ ବଦଳାଇବାକୁ **ମାନିଲା** 'the shopkeeper agreed to exchange it', … **ମାନିଲା ନାହିଁ** 'refused'. (ମନା କରିବା from unit 18 is a firmer 'refuse'.)

**Promised**: what they promised as a normal clause + **ବୋଲି** + **କଥା ଦେବା**: ସେମାନେ ସୋମବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା ଠିକ୍ କରିଦେବେ ବୋଲି **କଥା ଦେଇଛନ୍ତି** 'they've promised to fix it by Monday'. When the promises are empty: ଖାଲି **ଆଶ୍ୱାସନା** ଦେଉଛନ୍ତି 'all they give is promises'.

**Quoting the order itself** is also very common in speech: ସେ 'ଟିକେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରନ୍ତୁ' ବୋଲି କହିଲେ 'he said, "please wait a moment"'.

The trap: ସେ ମୋତେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା **କରିବାକୁ** କହିଲେ = he told *me* to wait; ସେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା **କରିବେ ବୋଲି** କହିଲେ = he said *he* would wait. The -ବାକୁ form is an instruction to the listener; a full verb + ବୋଲି is a statement.

examples.en: The police told me to come to the station.

examples.native: ବୋଉ ମୋତେ ରାତିରେ ଏକୁଟିଆ ନ ଯିବାକୁ କହିଲେ।

examples.en: Mum told me not to go out alone at night.

examples.roman: muṃ taṅku mo ṭôṅka pheraibaku ônurodhô kôli.
examples.en: I asked him to give my money back.
The shopkeeper refused to exchange it.

examples.native: ସେମାନେ ସୋମବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା ଠିକ୍ କରିଦେବେ ବୋଲି କଥା ଦେଇଛନ୍ତି।

dialogue.title: The wrong saree
dialogue.setting: Bhubaneswar, the week before Raja. Lipsa ordered a Sambalpuri saree in an online sale and something else arrived. She calls customer care while her flatmate Priyanka listens.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ନମସ୍କାର, ମୁଁ ରାହୁଲ କହୁଛି। କହନ୍ତୁ, କ'ଣ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିପାରିବି?
lines.roman: nômôskarô, muṃ Rahulô kôhuchhi. kôhôntu, kôṇô sahajjyô kôriparibi?
lines.en: Hello, this is Rahul speaking. How can I help?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ନମସ୍କାର। ମୁଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ବଲପୁରୀ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ମଗାଇଥିଲି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଗୋଟିଏ ସାଧା ପ୍ରିଣ୍ଟେଡ୍ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ଆସିଛି।
lines.roman: nômôskarô. muṃ goṭie Sômbôlôpuri saṛhi môgaithili, kintu goṭie sadha priṇṭeḍ saṛhi asichhi.
lines.en: Hello. I ordered a Sambalpuri saree, but a plain printed one has come.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ମାଫ କରିବେ ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍। ଆପଣଙ୍କ ଅର୍ଡର ନମ୍ବର କହିବେ?
lines.roman: maphô kôribe myaḍam. apôṇôṅkô ôrḍôr nômbôrô kôhibe?
lines.en: Sorry, ma'am. Could you give me your order number?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ମେସେଜ୍ କରିଛି। ଆଉ ପ୍ରମାଣ ପାଇଁ ଫଟୋ ବି ପଠାଇଛି।
lines.roman: mesej kôrichhi. au prômaṇô paiṃ phôṭo bi pôṭhaichhi.
lines.en: I've messaged it. And I've sent photos as proof too.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ଦେଖୁଛି… କିନ୍ତୁ ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍, ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ ସେଲର ଜିନିଷ ଫେରସ୍ତ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: dekhuchhi… kintu myaḍam, niyômô ônusare selôrô jinisô pherôstô hue nahiṃ.
lines.en: Let me see… but ma'am, as per the policy, sale items can't be returned.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ମୁଁ ବୁଝୁଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଏହା ମୋ ଭୁଲ ନୁହେଁ। ଆପଣମାନେ ଭୁଲ ଜିନିଷ ପଠାଇଛନ୍ତି।
lines.roman: muṃ bujhuchhi, kintu eha mo bhulô nuheṃ. apôṇômane bhulô jinisô pôṭhaichhônti.
lines.en: I understand, but this isn't my mistake. You've sent the wrong item.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ହଁ, ସେଇଟା ଠିକ୍… ଟିକେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରନ୍ତୁ, ମୁଁ ମୋ ସିନିୟରଙ୍କୁ ପଚାରୁଛି।

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍, କାଲି ଆମ ଲୋକ ଆସି ଶାଢ଼ୀ ନେଇଯିବେ। ସାତ ଦିନରେ ଟଙ୍କା ଫେରିବ, ନହେଲେ ଆପଣ ଠିକ୍ ଶାଢ଼ୀଟି ନେଇପାରିବେ।

lines.en: Ma'am, our person will come and collect the saree tomorrow. You'll get the money back in seven days — or you can have the right saree.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ଟଙ୍କା ନୁହେଁ, ମୋତେ ସେଇ ସମ୍ବଲପୁରୀ ଶାଢ଼ୀଟି ହିଁ ଦରକାର। ରଜ ପାଇଁ ମଗାଇଥିଲି।
lines.roman: ṭôṅka nuheṃ, mote sei Sômbôlôpuri saṛhiṭi hiṃ dôrôkarô. Rôjô paiṃ môgaithili.
lines.en: Not the money — I want that Sambalpuri saree. I ordered it for Raja.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.native: ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି। ଆପଣଙ୍କ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ନମ୍ବର ମେସେଜରେ ଆସିଯିବ। ଆଉ କିଛି?
lines.roman: ṭhik ôchhi. apôṇôṅkô ôbhijogô nômbôrô mesejôre asijibô. au kichhi?
lines.en: All right. Your complaint number will come by text. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Priyanka
lines.en: So what did they say? Did they agree to a refund?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ପ୍ରଥମେ କହିଲେ ସେଲର ଜିନିଷ ଫେରସ୍ତ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ। ମୁଁ ଶାନ୍ତରେ ବୁଝାଇଲି, ତା'ପରେ ଠିକ୍ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ପଠାଇବେ ବୋଲି କଥା ଦେଲେ। ଦେଖିବା!
lines.roman: prôthôme kôhile selôrô jinisô pherôstô hue nahiṃ. muṃ santôre bujhaili, tapôre ṭhik saṛhi pôṭhaibe boli kôtha dele. dekhiba!
lines.en: First they said sale items can't be returned. I explained calmly, and then they promised to send the right saree. We'll see!

culture:
When something goes wrong, the approach that works in Odisha is **polite persistence**: start soft (ଦୟାକରି ଟିକେ ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ), explain clearly, repeat yourself calmly, and if you get nowhere ask for the **ସିନିୟର୍**. Raising your voice (**ପାଟି କରିବା**) usually makes things slower, especially with officials — the person in front of you suddenly discovers a rule (**ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ…**). A little humour and a respectful **ସାର୍ / ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍ / ଭାଇନା** go a long way.

Helplines usually start in Hindi and English; some offer Odia, and you can always ask **ଓଡ଼ିଆରେ କଥା ହୋଇପାରିବି କି?** Agents and customers alike mix in English freely — ଅର୍ଡର, ରିଫଣ୍ଡ, ଏକ୍ସଚେଞ୍ଜ, କମ୍ପ୍ଲେନ୍ — with Odia verbs around them.

If your phone is lost or stolen: block the SIM with your operator, report it at the local police station (**ଥାନା**) — a lost report or an **ଏଫଆଇଆର୍** — and then block the handset through the government's Sanchar Saathi (CEIR) website using that report. Take ID (Aadhaar or passport), address the officer as **ସାର୍** or **ଆଜ୍ଞା**, and expect to be asked to come back. With an overcharging auto driver, most locals argue briefly and with a smile, settle on a figure, and move on — **ଝଗଡ଼ା କରି କିଛି ଲାଭ ନାହିଁ**.

tip.title: Returns and exchanges
tip.body:
- To order (have sent): **ମଗାଇବା** — ଅନଲାଇନ୍ ମଗାଇଥିଲି.
- To return: **ଫେରସ୍ତ କରିବା**; can it be returned? **ଫେରସ୍ତ କରି ହେବ କି?**
- Instead: X **ବଦଳରେ** — ଏହା ବଦଳରେ ନୂଆ ଗୋଟିଏ.
- Describe first, then ask — no need to sound angry.

tip.title: They said… they asked…
tip.body:
- Keep the original tense: ସେ କହିଲେ ଟଙ୍କା **ଫେରିବ** 'they said it *would* come back'.
- **ଯେ** after the verb, or **ବୋଲି** before it: ସେ କହିଲେ **ଯେ** … · … **ବୋଲି** କହିଲା.
- Yes/no questions: **କି ନାହିଁ** 'whether'; others keep the question word: **କେବେ** ଆସିବ.
- Casual: ସେ **କହୁଥିଲେ** 'he was saying'.

lessons.title: He told me to…, they promised…

tip.title: Told me to · agreed to · promised
tip.body:
- Told me to: **ମୋତେ** … **-ବାକୁ କହିଲେ**; not to: **ନ** -ବାକୁ.
- Agreed / refused: -ବାକୁ **ମାନିଲେ** / **ମାନିଲେ ନାହିଁ**.
- Promised: clause + **ବୋଲି କଥା ଦେଲେ**.
- Trap: ମୋତେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରି**ବାକୁ** କହିଲେ (me) ≠ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରି**ବେ ବୋଲି** କହିଲେ (he).

tip.title: At the police station
tip.body:
- Use **ଆପଣ** and **ସାର୍ / ଆଜ୍ଞା** with officers.
- 'I want to file an FIR': **ଏଫଆଇଆର୍ କରିବାକୁ ଚାହେଁ**.

- Expect instructions: ବିଲ୍ ଆଣି**ବାକୁ** କହିଲେ.

tip.title: Firm, not loud
tip.body:

- Ripped off: ମୋତେ **ଠକିଦେଲା** (ଦେବା adds 'it happened to me').
- Demand your due: ଏହା ମୋର **ଦାବି**, ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ.

sentences.native: ଏହା ମୋର ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ, ଏହା ନିୟମ।
sentences.roman: eha morô dabi nuheṃ, eha niyômô.
sentences.en: This isn't just me demanding it — it's the rule.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଭାବିଲି ଦୋକାନୀ ମୋତେ ଠକୁଛି।
sentences.roman: muṃ bhabili dokani mote ṭhôkuchhi.
sentences.en: I thought the shopkeeper was cheating me.

sentences.native: ଝଗଡ଼ା କରି କିଛି ଲାଭ ନାହିଁ, ଚାଲ ଯିବା।
sentences.roman: jhôgôṛa kôri kichhi labhô nahiṃ, chalô jiba.
sentences.en: No point fighting — let's go.

sentences.native: ସେ ମୋ ଉପରେ ପାଟି କଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ମୁଁ ଶାନ୍ତ ରହିଲି।
sentences.roman: se mo upôre paṭi kôla, kintu muṃ santô rôhili.
sentences.en: He shouted at me, but I stayed calm.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ଭୁଲ ପାଇଁ ମୋର କ୍ଷତି କାହିଁକି ହେବ?
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkô bhulô paiṃ morô khyôti kahiṃki hebô?
sentences.en: Why should I lose out because of your mistake?
